newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nordic states launch plan to beat warring bikers.
newsitem.headline: Nordic states launch plan to beat warring bikers.

text.p: The Nordic countries are to tighten cross-border efforts to deal with warring motorcycle gangs which have caused havoc in normally peaceful Scandinavia, the Swedish and Norwegian justice ministries said on Friday.

The Nordic nations have agreed on a plan to boost police links and find legislative means to fight the rival Hell's Angels and Bandidos motorcycle gangs whose turf war has claimed 10 lives over the past three years.
However, they remained divided on whether or not to outlaw the gangs.
"This cooperation has started and is going on at a very intensive level but will increase on specific questions," a spokesman for the Swedish Justice Ministry told Reuters.

A Norwegian Justice Ministry spokeswoman said the plan, drawn up by the five Nordic nations' justice ministers this week, was backed by their prime ministers at a meeting in the western Norwegian town of Bergen on Thursday.
Under the plan, Norway will take responsibility for cooperation with the other states and initiate a region-wide police strategy.
Denmark will form a steering group to fight the international criminal activities of the motorcycle gangs.
"It is more like intentions which each country has to implement," said the spokeswoman.
New police efforts will also involve setting up analysis groups to track the bikers' activities and boosting witness protection schemes for informants from the biker clans.
But the countries are still split on whether to ban the gangs, whose bitter turf war began in 1993 when the Bandidos challenged the Hells Angels' Nordic dominance.
The battle has involved the use of missiles and bombs and is one of the most serious crime problems faced by the Nordic governments.
Norway's Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland vowed to crack down on the gangs after a woman bystander was killed on June 5 in the bombing of a Bandidos clubhouse in Drammen, Norway.
The spokesman for the Swedish Justice Ministry said Denmark was considering applying to the biker gangs legislation that banned organisations with violence as a purpose.
But he said neither Sweden nor Norway had this kind of legislation, which would go against their constitutions.
"But we are following the Danish situation to see if this would be an effective means or not," the spokesman said.
Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson has expressed opposition to banning motorcycle gangs in any of the Nordic countries, saying it would just exacerbate the problems for neighbouring countries.
